rules.title: Aggregate return types are returned by value
rules.statement: A function whose return type is a tuple, struct, ZonedStruct, or payload-carrying (tagged) enum returns the aggregate by value (as a value of the aggregate's storage type), never as a pointer to function-local storage; this guarantees the returned value outlives the callee frame.

rules.title: Payload-free enum returns as i32
rules.statement: A function returning a C-style enum (an enum with no payload variants, so no tagged-enum layout) returns its discriminant as a 32-bit integer rather than an aggregate.

rules.title: Reference-kind return ABI determined by RefRepr descriptor
rules.statement: When the return type is a reference kind, its by-value return representation is the reference's RefRepr: dyn-trait and slice references return their 16-byte fat (pointer,metadata) pair by value; closure / custom-DST / thin references return their 8-byte value pointer.

rules.title: AnyVal is represented as a 32-bit value
rules.statement: A value of type AnyVal is represented as a 32-bit integer in both parameter and return position.
rules.uncertainty: i32 likely encodes a handle/index into an AnyVal table; exact semantics inferred from representation only.

rules.title: Array parameters are passed by pointer
rules.statement: A parameter whose type is an array [T; N] is passed by pointer (to the array storage), not by value.

rules.title: Variadic functions are extern-only C-ABI declarations
rules.statement: A function declared variadic (vararg) is emitted only as an external declaration with C variadic calling convention; non-vararg parameters are typed normally and a missing return type denotes void.

rules.title: Each mangled function symbol must have at most one body
rules.statement: Two distinct functions resolving to the same mangled link symbol is an error; in particular a private function in one package and a pub function of the same base name in an imported package must not collide, requiring rename to disambiguate.

rules.title: Methods are emitted under module-qualified link symbols
rules.statement: A function's emitted link symbol is its module-qualified name: methods gain the module prefix; free functions and extern functions keep their bare name. Symbol identity and forward-declaration deduplication key off this link name.

rules.title: Void function body may fall through to an implicit return
rules.statement: A function with no return type (void) whose body reaches the end without an explicit terminator returns implicitly; a non-void function reaching the end without returning is a reachability error rejected earlier in semantic analysis.
